## Tokyo Business Trip Overview: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12

A practical 3-day plan for **2 adults** with a hotel target of **under 28,000 JPY per night**. I’ve kept the schedule business-first, added a **client dinner on Mar 10**, a **half-day sightseeing window on Mar 11**, and protected enough time for a **15:40 airport departure on Mar 12**.

## Day-by-Day Tokyo Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival, Check-in, and Client Dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- 10:00–12:30: Arrive in Tokyo, clear immigration, and transfer to hotel
  - Transit buffer: 60–90 minutes for airport formalities
  - Recommended hotel zones: **Shinagawa, Tokyo Station, Shinjuku, or Ginza** for easy business access
- 12:30–14:00: Early lunch near hotel and light reset
  - Meal idea: soba set, tonkatsu, or a quick teishoku lunch
- 14:00–17:30: Check-in, freshen up, and prepare for meeting
  - Buffer: 30 minutes before leaving for dinner venue
- 18:30–21:00: **Client dinner**
  - Best style: private dining room, kaiseki, sushi counter, or modern izakaya with quiet seating
  - Suggested areas: **Ginza, Marunouchi, Nihonbashi, or Roppongi**
- 21:00–22:00: Return to hotel and decompress

### Day 2: Business Morning, Half-Day Sightseeing, and Flexible Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- 07:00–08:00: Breakfast at hotel
  - Keep it simple: rice, eggs, fish, miso soup, fruit
- 08:30–12:00: Business meetings or work block
  - Transit buffer: 20–30 minutes between office, café, or meeting sites
- 12:00–13:00: Lunch near the meeting area
  - Meal idea: ramen, curry rice, or a set lunch in a business district
- 13:30–17:30: **Half-day sightseeing**
  - Best low-friction options: Asakusa, Imperial Palace area, Tokyo Station Marunouchi, or Shibuya Scramble area
  - Keep the route compact to avoid cross-city transit fatigue
- 17:30–18:30: Return to hotel and rest
- 19:00–20:30: Dinner or light networking
  - If energy is low: choose a nearby sushi bar, tempura, or yakitori spot
- 20:30 onward: Pack essentials and confirm departure logistics

### Day 3: Check-out and Airport Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

- 07:00–08:00: Breakfast and final room check
- 08:00–10:30: Final work block, email catch-up, or short meeting
  - Keep luggage packed and ready by 10:00
- 10:30–11:30: Check-out and store any remaining items if needed
- 11:30–13:00: Early lunch near station or hotel
  - Meal idea: donburi, udon, or a quick bento
- 13:00–13:30: Depart for airport
  - Transit buffer: aim to leave city center **at least 4 hours before departure**
- 15:40: Flight departure

## Hotel Budget-Friendly Stay Plan

For **under 28,000 JPY per night**, these Tokyo areas are the safest fit for business travel:

- **Shinagawa**: strong rail access, efficient for airport transfers
- **Tokyo Station / Marunouchi**: best for corporate convenience, usually pricier but can fit with early booking
- **Shinjuku**: good value and many business hotels
- **Ginza / Nihonbashi**: polished and central, but rates vary widely

A realistic target is a **business hotel or compact full-service hotel** with:
- twin or double room
- Wi‑Fi
- breakfast optional
- laundry access or coin laundry nearby
- easy station access

## Packing Checklist for 2 Adults

### Business Essentials
- Passport and travel documents
- Flight details and hotel confirmation
- Work laptop, charger, phone charger, power bank
- Business cards
- Meeting notes, presentation files, adapter if needed

### Clothing
- 2–3 business outfits
- 1 smart-casual dinner outfit
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Lightweight outer layer for March weather
- Socks and undergarments for 3 days
- Optional umbrella or compact rain jacket

### Personal Items
- Toiletries and skincare
- Medications and vitamins
- Hand sanitizer and tissues
- Small umbrella
- Reusable water bottle

### Useful Extras
- Portable luggage scale
- Snacks for transit
- Spare mask if preferred
- Small gift if the client dinner is formal

## Transit Buffers and Timing Tips

- Build in **30–45 minutes** for most city transfers
- Build in **60–90 minutes** for airport check-in and security
- For the final day, avoid scheduling anything after **13:00**
- Keep sightseeing on Mar 11 geographically tight so it does not interfere with work or dinner

## Sources

- Tokyo travel and transit planning: https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html
- Tokyo airport access and departure planning: https://www.tokyo-airport-bus.co.jp/en/
- Tokyo visitor information: https://www.gotokyo.org/en/
